classification.difficultyReason: Scaffolded line equations, intersection, midpoint and perpendicular-gradient checks establish familiar rhombus properties.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Use the results of part a to find the coordinates of the point of intersection of $AC$ and $BD$.

answer.worked:
Substitute $y=\frac12x+\frac72$ into $y=-2x+16$:
$$\begin{align*}\frac12x+\frac72&=-2x+16\\x+7&=-4x+32\\5x&=25\\x&=5\\y&=-2(5)+16\\y&=6\end{align*}$$
The point of intersection is $(5,6)$. Check: $\frac12(5)+\frac72=6$ and $-2(5)+16=6$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Show that the point of intersection is the midpoint of both $AC$ and $BD$ and that $AC$ is perpendicular to $BD$.

answer.short: Both midpoints are $(5,6)$, and $m_{AC}m_{BD}=\frac12(-2)=-1$, so $AC\perp BD$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}M_{AC}&=\left(\frac{1+9}{2},\frac{4+8}{2}\right)\\M_{AC}&=(5,6)\\M_{BD}&=\left(\frac{4+6}{2},\frac{8+4}{2}\right)\\M_{BD}&=(5,6)\end{align*}$$
Both midpoints equal the intersection found in part b.
$$\begin{align*}m_{AC}m_{BD}&=\frac12\times(-2)\\m_{AC}m_{BD}&=-1\end{align*}$$
The product of the gradients is $-1$, so $AC$ is perpendicular to $BD$.
